expectations.text: Output warns that a single Louvain run reflects modularity DEGENERACY — many qualitatively different partitions have near-equal modularity (Good et al.) — not just random stochasticity
expectations.evidence: Response mentioned that 'results can vary between runs due to randomness in the greedy optimization' and recommended a fixed random seed, but did not identify or name modularity degeneracy as a conceptual problem — the idea that many structurally different partitions share near-equal Q. Good et al. was not referenced.

expectations.text: Output frames stability analysis as a PREREQUISITE before naming or interpreting communities, not as an optional improvement step
expectations.evidence: Stability was mentioned only as a brief caveat in step 7 ('Louvain is a heuristic algorithm and results can vary'), placed after extensive naming/reporting guidance. The response proceeded immediately to naming instructions without requiring stability to be established first.

expectations.text: Output recommends running community detection many times (e.g., 100+ runs) and measuring pairwise stability with ARI, NMI, or similar
expectations.evidence: No recommendation to run the algorithm multiple times was made. ARI, NMI, and similar partition-agreement metrics were not mentioned at all.

expectations.text: Output recommends comparing Q = 0.67 against a configuration-model null (random graphs with the same degree sequence) rather than accepting it at face value
expectations.evidence: The response called Q = 0.67 'quite high' and accepted it at face value. No comparison against a configuration-model null or randomized baseline was suggested.

expectations.text: Output mentions Louvain resolution limit or the alternative of SBM (Stochastic Block Model) for more principled partitioning
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly mentioned the resolution limit: 'Modularity optimization can exhibit a resolution limit (Fortunato & Barthélemy, 2007), meaning very small tightly-knit subgroups within larger communities may be merged.' SBM was not mentioned.
